title: Pixel Cookie consent mode
content_data:
TikTok's pixel consent mode offers two solutions: - Default opt-out solution: This solution will prevent pixels from sharing data with TikTok until user consent is explicitly granted. - Default opt-in solution: This solution will allow pixels to share data with TikTok until user consent is explicitly revoked. # Default opt-out solution 1. In pixel base code, add "holdConsent", "revokeConsent" and "grantConsent" in the `ttq.methods` array. 2. Call `ttq.holdConsent()` before loading the pixel via `ttq.load()`. This will queue events but not share them until the user consent status changes. 3. Based on the user's preference: - If users grant consent, call `ttq.grantConsent()`. This will share events to the TikTok server, including events that were previously queued in the session. - If users reject consent, call `ttq.revokeConsent()`. This will prevent events from being shared to the TikTok server, including previously queued events in that session. 4. If users change their preference, call `ttq.grantConsent()` or `ttq.revokeConsent()` as applicable to either enable or disable data sharing via the pixel. Calling `ttq.revokeConsent()` does not affect data shared with the TikTok server. > **Note**
> Where applicable, advertisers should implement this solution on every webpage where they've installed the TikTok pixel. **Use case 1: Websites default to opt-out before users make an explicit selection** ```xcodeblock (code Javascript javascript) (/code) ``` ``` xcodeblock (code) // Users explicitly reject cookies ttq.revokeConsent() // After a certain period // ... // Users accept them later ttq.grantConsent() (/code) ```
